assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks have made an exceptional advance in the control and measurement of atomic quantum systems, with fundamental and far-reaching consequences.
assessment.attribution: Katori originated the magic-wavelength lattice-clock concept and Ye made decisive experimental realizations and developments.
assessment.maturity: Independent laboratories now operate clocks of extraordinary reproducibility and accuracy, with clear scientific uses beyond timekeeping.
uncertainties: The relative credit for subsequent clock architectures and enabling metrology advances requires careful delimitation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The recognition that quantum phases can have observable physical consequences changed the conceptual and practical understanding of quantum mechanics.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov's work identified the physical significance of potentials, while Berry established the general geometrical phase framework.
assessment.maturity: The effects are extensively tested across atomic, optical, condensed-matter, and interferometric systems.
uncertainties: The candidate joins related but historically distinct effects, so the scientific narrative must not overstate a single shared discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light converts a basic quantum feature of radiation into a demonstrable gain in precision, including gravitational-wave interferometry.
assessment.attribution: Caves provided a central quantum-measurement framework, while Mavalvala and Schnabel made decisive experimental and interferometric contributions.
assessment.maturity: Noise reduction below the standard quantum limit is reproducible and has become operational in major precision experiments.
uncertainties: The full experimental lineage includes several important laboratories and may be difficult to compress into three awardees.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: SASE X-ray free-electron lasers opened a qualitatively new means of observing ultrafast structure and dynamics at atomic length scales.
assessment.attribution: The named scientists represent key theoretical, accelerator, and realization contributions to the SASE X-ray laser.
assessment.maturity: The principle has been realized at multiple major facilities and has enabled a broad, sustained experimental field.
uncertainties: Large-facility development involved extensive collective contributions, making individual attribution demanding.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold-atom realizations of Hubbard physics created a highly controllable route to addressing important quantum-many-body problems.
assessment.attribution: Bloch, Greiner, and Esslinger led foundational experimental advances; the theory-to-experiment connection is essential to the achievement.
assessment.maturity: Many laboratories have reproduced and extended quantum simulations with increasing control and diagnostic power.
uncertainties: Whether the platform has yet delivered a decisive solution to a major many-body problem remains open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry made coherent matter waves into an unusually precise probe of gravity, motion, and fundamental quantum physics.
assessment.attribution: The proposed names made influential early conceptual and experimental contributions to modern atom-interferometric methods.
assessment.maturity: The techniques are well established, broadly replicated, and central to precision atomic physics.
uncertainties: The foundational work is distributed across a broad community, and the precise boundary of the prizeable invention needs scrutiny.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg blockade made strong, programmable interactions between individually controlled neutral atoms a powerful new quantum platform.
assessment.attribution: Saffman developed central blockade and gate concepts, while Lukin and Browaeys led landmark experimental platforms and demonstrations.
assessment.maturity: Neutral-atom arrays are now replicated in several laboratories and show impressive control, simulation, and computing capabilities.
uncertainties: The field remains rapidly developing, and a durable fundamental breakthrough beyond the platform itself is still being tested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: KPZ universality revealed a striking common structure in far-from-equilibrium growth, linking theory, scaling, and precise experiment.
assessment.attribution: Kardar and Zhang introduced the defining equation, and Takeuchi supplied especially compelling quantitative experimental tests.
assessment.maturity: The universality class has accumulated broad theoretical, numerical, and experimental support over decades.
uncertainties: Its wide applicability can make the most direct physical discovery and the appropriate experimental credit difficult to define.
